ruleCards.title: På fredag, på fredagar, i fredags
ruleCards.rule: På + day = this coming day. På + day + -ar = every week on that day. I + day + -s = last week’s day (it’s over).
examples: See you on Friday (this coming one).
I fredags var jag i Åbo.
Last Friday I was in Turku.
ruleCards.watch: Days are written with a small letter: måndag, tisdag, onsdag, torsdag, fredag, lördag, söndag.

ruleCards.title: Numbers 0–12
ruleCards.rule: Learn the first numbers by heart. The number one is en or ett, matching the noun.
examples: noll, en/ett, två, tre, fyra, fem, sex
sju, åtta, nio, tio, elva, tolv
ruleCards.watch: Counting on its own you say ett: ett, två, tre.

ruleCards.title: Teens: -ton
ruleCards.watch: Look out for fjorton (14, not fyrton) and arton (18, not åtton).

ruleCards.title: Tens: -tio
ruleCards.rule: Most tens end in -tio. Put the small number straight after the ten, as one word.
ruleCards.watch: Tjugo (20) is the odd one out: it ends in -o. Don’t mix up trettio (30) and tretton (13).

ruleCards.title: Dates: den sjätte december
ruleCards.rule: Say dates with den + ordinal number + month. In writing you can use the digit: den 6 december.
examples: Idag är det den sjätte december.
Today is the sixth of December.
Jag fyller år den tredje maj.
My birthday is on the third of May.
ruleCards.watch: No “of”: den 6 december, not den 6 av december.

ruleCards.title: Months
ruleCards.rule: Months are written with a small letter. Use i for “in”: i maj.
examples: januari, februari, mars, april, maj, juni
juli, augusti, september, oktober, november, december
Vi reser till Sverige i juli.
We’re travelling to Sweden in July.
ruleCards.watch: Small letter mid-sentence: i juli, not i Juli.

ruleCards.title: The weather
ruleCards.rule: Weather sentences usually start with det. The sun is the exception: solen skiner.
ruleCards.watch: Det blåser is a verb: no är. Det är blåsigt also works.
